Hi all — I ran the heatmap and sample traces for Aptiva's August window. Below is a short technical summary (TL;DR then detail).

TL;DR: Our runtime applied the 16-token minimum quantum per request for calls that did not find a hot KV-cache prefix within a 60s rolling affinity window. Many of Aptiva's hooks are rapid, short prompts and they didn't hit prefix reuse often in August — that produced a systematic uplift. We can credibly reverse-charge ~45% of the uplift for August because the behavior is reproducible and we logged the request-level token counts.

Details:
- Billing rule in effect (Aug 1–31): quantum = 16 tokens, rolling affinity window = 60s, per-API-key aggregation only when the same context prefix hash appears in the last 60s on the same host.
- Why charges look inflated: Calls with <16 tokens are rounded up to 16 unless the runtime aggregates them into an active conversation cache. For Aptiva we observed ~12k short calls; ~7.4k lacked an active prefix and were billed at 16 rather than their true token length.
- Calculation (sample): total billed uplift = sum(16 - actual_tokens) over those requests = ~2,560,000 token-units = equivalent to $3,240 at their SKU rates. Our suggested one-time adjustment = $3,240 * 0.45 = $1,458 (we recommend partial goodwill and a config change to avoid recurrence).

Attached: rounding_calc_Aptiva.xlsx (worked example + SQL snippets).

Proposed remediation:
1) Issue a one-time credit equal to the proposed amount while we convert Aptiva to a lower-quantum pilot (temporary quantum = 8 tokens for 30 days) to validate behavioral change.
2) Add an invoice line showing "quantum-rounding adjustments" with a link to a short report for transparency (helps procurement teams).

Camila — let me know if you want me to draft the report or if Finance should run the credit.

— Sergio
